native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 (n=289), 1985 composite wealth is low overall (median $720; 25th-pct $0; ≈5% in debt) but shows clear demographic disparities in the prospective/pre-incarceration sense. Race is the dominant gradient: White median $2,200 (IQR $0–$9,100, 8.7% negative) >> Black median $320 (IQR $0–$4,700, 4.4% negative) ≈ Hispanic median $0 (IQR $0–$5,500, 4.9% negative). Wilcoxon rank-sum confirms white > black (Δmedian +$1,880, p=0.046) and white > hispanic (Δmedian +$2,200, p=0.041); black ≈ hispanic (p=0.58). Sex is secondary but real: men median $1,000 vs women median $0 (Wilcoxon p=0.024). Race × sex intersections are exploratory due to small female cells (n=9, 12, 16); among men the white > black ≈ hispanic pattern holds (medians $2,000 / $800 / $700). Quantile regression at q=0.5 corroborates: Black main effect ≈ −$1,200 (p=0.051), Black×Female interaction ≈ −$3,350 (p=0.038). Context: never-jailed reference cohort (n=11,724) has median $3,600, five times higher than the ever-jailed cohort, p≈1.6×10⁻¹⁰.
native_result.WorkflowB: (1) Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 × 6, 0 missing). (2) Normalised race label typo 'hipanic' → 'hispanic'. (3) Filtered to ever_jailed==1 (n=289). (4) Built per-cell median+Q1+Q3+IQR+%neg tables by race, sex, and race×sex; same for ever_jailed==0 reference cohort (n=11,724). (5) Within ever_jailed==1, ran Kruskal-Wallis (race) and Wilcoxon rank-sum (race pairwise and sex), plus quantile regression at q=0.5 with race+sex+interaction. (6) Negative wealth retained (debt-inclusive). (7) Saved all tables and qreg summary to analysis/output/.
